title: Landfall and Monsoon
premise: Casper Sandoval, a disgraced railroad engineer hiding in a river town under a false name, is the only person who knows the closed mountain lines well enough to reach an expedition that has gone silent beyond the pass. Pressed by the expedition's financier and haunted by her own role in a fatal bridge collapse she was blamed for, she agrees to lead a small party upriver and over the range before the early snows seal it. Along the way she discovers the expedition wasn't lost by accident—it was sabotaged to bury evidence of forced labor on the railroad's new extension. The book ends with Casper choosing to surrender her anonymity, testifying to what she knows at the cost of her freedom, but winning justice for the dead and, finally, a place among the people she crossed the mountains with.
about_author: Emrys Reyes is the pen name of a former surveyor who spent a decade mapping rail corridors through remote mountain country before turning to fiction. Their novels are known for technical precision, unforgiving landscapes, and characters who must decide what survival is actually worth.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgot Her Name
chapters.summary: POV Casper. In the river town of Puerto Vado, Casper works odd jobs under an assumed name, keeping her engineer's past buried. A debt collector finds her anyway. The beat is wary isolation—the fragile peace of someone always ready to run.

chapters.title: Silence on Channel Nine
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The financier, Ilsa Marchetti, arrives: her upriver survey expedition has missed three radio check-ins. She offers Casper double her debt to guide a rescue party along the closed line. Casper refuses. The beat is dread—she recognizes the route and what it costs.

chapters.title: What the Bridge Took
chapters.summary: POV Casper, flashback-woven. The collector sells Casper's real identity to Marchetti, forcing her hand. We learn of the Viaduct 7 collapse that ended her career and killed eleven men—a verdict she has never accepted. Beat: grief weaponized into leverage.

chapters.title: A Crew of Strangers
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Marchetti assembles the party: gruff boatman Teo, medic Ruth Okafor, and Marchetti's nephew Dario, whose enthusiasm outruns his sense. They load the launch and leave at dawn. Beat: uneasy fellowship among people with separate reasons for going.

chapters.title: Upriver
chapters.summary: POV Teo. The river narrows; abandoned logging camps appear, stripped years ago. Teo reads the water and the crew, sensing Dario is reporting back to his aunt by hidden radio. Beat: the journey stops being rescue and starts feeling like surveillance.

chapters.title: The First Marker
chapters.summary: POV Casper. At the junction of the closed line they find a fresh survey marker—newer than anything official. Someone has been working this 'abandoned' corridor within the year. Beat: suspicion hardens into certainty that the expedition found something it wasn't meant to find.

chapters.title: Camp Ash
chapters.summary: POV Ruth. They reach the expedition's last camp, burned, supplies intact but radios smashed deliberately. One survivor's note points higher into the pass. Ruth treats a wounded laborer left behind, who whispers about quotas and chains. Beat: horror replacing urgency.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wouldn't Leave
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The laborer, Emilio, recovers enough to talk: the new extension uses conscripted workers, and the survey team photographed the camps. Casper realizes Marchetti may have sent them not to rescue but to confirm nothing survived. Beat: betrayal dawning.

chapters.title: Weather Turning
chapters.summary: POV Teo. An early storm front builds over the range. Teo argues for turning back; Dario insists on pressing on, radioing coordinates to someone below. Casper catches him mid-transmission. Beat: open fracture inside the party.

chapters.title: The Switchback Road
chapters.summary: POV Casper. They abandon the boat and climb onto the old closed-line grade, Casper reading decayed trestles and tunnel mouths from memory. A rope bridge fails; Ruth saves Dario at risk to herself. Beat: competence as trust—Casper's knowledge becomes their lifeline.

chapters.title: Tunnel Nine
chapters.summary: POV Ruth. Sheltering overnight in a half-collapsed tunnel, Emilio shows them a hidden side gallery where workers scratched names into rock. Ruth photographs every one. Beat: the dead become individuals; the mission gains a conscience.

chapters.title: Dario's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Dario. Cornered, Dario admits Marchetti knew about the labor camps all along; the expedition's disappearance was convenient. He's been feeding her their position so her men can intercept any evidence. Beat: guilt and a first flicker of defiance—he chooses to stop transmitting.

chapters.title: Men on the Grade
chapters.summary: POV Teo. Marchetti's hired crew ambushes them at a washout, demanding the expedition's film canisters. A running fight along the grade; Teo takes a bullet graze covering the others' escape into the treeline. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Above the Treeline
chapters.summary: POV Casper. With pursuers behind and snow ahead, Casper leads a brutal ascent she once surveyed and swore never to walk again. Supplies dwindle; tempers fray. Beat: endurance stripped to essentials—she stops leading strangers and starts leading family.

chapters.title: What Casper Buried
chapters.summary: POV Casper. In a high camp, Casper confesses the truth of Viaduct 7: she flagged the flawed piers and was overruled, then scapegoated. She ran instead of fighting. Beat: catharsis—the debt she carries was never hers alone.

chapters.title: The Silent Camp
chapters.summary: POV Ruth. They find the expedition alive but starving in a high basin, leader injured, film and ledgers intact. Marchetti's men are a day behind. Beat: relief shadowed by arithmetic—not everyone can move fast enough to outrun the snow.

chapters.title: Snowfall
chapters.summary: POV Teo. The front hits. Teo stays behind with the slowest survivors at a shelter cave, buying time he may not survive. Beat: sacrifice offered freely, the theme of belonging answered by action rather than words.

chapters.title: The Descent
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper leads the rest down the far side through whiteout, navigating by counting switchbacks against the wind, using a trick from her old survey days. Two close calls, no losses. Beat: mastery reclaimed—her exile's skills become salvation.

chapters.title: Marchetti's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Casper. At the valley railhead, Marchetti waits with police and lawyers, offering Casper full exoneration for Viaduct 7 if the ledgers burn. Everything Casper wanted, priced at the eleven names in Tunnel Nine. Beat: temptation crystallized.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper refuses, publicly hands the ledgers and Tunnel Nine photographs to a waiting journalist and railway inspector, naming Marchetti and accepting her own reckoning. Marchetti's men scatter. Beat: justice chosen outside every safe option.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Ruth. Weeks later, hearings open. Casper testifies to both crimes—the cover-up and her own silence after Viaduct 7. Teo, recovered, sits beside Emilio and the rescued workers. Beat: accountability as the only honest form of belonging.

chapters.title: Open Line
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Sentenced to supervised service rebuilding mountain bridges, Casper walks a restored grade with her new crew, compass in hand, map of open lines now. Beat: quiet resolution—she stopped being invisible and became, at last, someone counted.
